requirements.text: For each roadway network it maintains, the Center shall provide the following information: 1. Network identifier, 2. Network name, 3. Number of links in the network, 4. Number of nodes in the network, 5. List of link data, 6. List of node data.

The Center shall provide the following link information: 1. Link identifier, 2. Link name, 3. Road number, 4. Link type, 5. Link type description, 6. Start node, 7. End node, 8. Direction, 9. Length, 10. Capacity, 11. Speed limit, 12. Speed limit truck, 13. Number of lanes.

The Center shall provide the following node information: 1. Node identifier, 2. Node name, 3. Node jurisdiction, 4. Owner, 5. Latitude/longitude, 6. Type of node (i.e., intersection or bridge), 7. Node type description, 8. Number of links.
The Data Collector shall be designed to support the storage of TMDD data elements and message set information.
The C2C Project shall utilize the TMDD standard (including message sets) to transmit information.
DATEX/ASN shall be used to transmit the TMDD message sets.
TCP/IP shall be used to transmit the DATEX/ASN data.
The C2C Server shall execute in a Microsoft Windows NT environment.
A DATEX/ASN runtime library shall be available on any computer communicating to the C2C project.
The C2C shall be implemented in the C/C++ programming language.
The system shall implement encrypted authentication (e.g., TLS/SSL) for all remote control GUI sessions and enforce role-based access control (RBAC) for all device command/control operations.
The system shall implement a secure gateway or VPN for all external connections, ensuring that no direct access to internal TMC devices is exposed to the public network.
All device control commands shall include a unique transaction ID and a timestamp to prevent replay attacks, and all command messages shall be digitally signed or authenticated to ensure integrity.
The C2C system shall maintain 99.9% availability during peak traffic hours and provide automated reconnection logic for TCP/IP sessions within 30 seconds of a link failure.
The system shall process and propagate device control commands within 500ms and update status information across the network within 2 seconds of receipt.
The system shall implement a priority-based locking mechanism for device control, where a 'master' center is defined for each device and override requests are logged with timestamp and origin.
The system shall support a minimum of 500 concurrent field devices and 50 simultaneous remote GUI connections without exceeding 70% CPU utilization on the C2C Server.
The system shall ensure that test mode operations are logically isolated from production databases and that test traffic is clearly tagged to prevent accidental control of field devices.
